I disagree with "editorialized" titles but the /v/news mods have been known to call the original article's title "editorializing", or call using the most interesting quote from the article "editorializing". There are some articles with all-caps in the headlines that will get deleted (No caps rule) if you keep the original title and be considered "editorialized" if you alter the title. So yeah, if the title is quoted/paraphrased from the article itself without "adding" incendiary BS, I think it allows us room to create more descriptive titles than the original, without starting a war between story spinners. In reality we already have wars between the story spinners, but they try to downvote other people posting the same story from a different source to +1 points (to keep the post invisible). In the end the votes decide what slants are acceptable and which are too heavy-handed.

How to Turn Your Old Laptop into a Chromebook

CloudReady runs okay on my '09 netbook, and it's only got an Atom N455 1.66GHz and 2GB of RAM. There are still a number of bugs, but if you want something simple it's a great way to breathe new life into an old laptop.
I run Xubuntu 14.04 on my 2009 netbook with worse specs and it runs fine.

I switched to Arch Linux using LXDE and it runs much better than CloudReady, even with using Chromium. I was happy with CloudReady for the most part, but it didn't have the basic functionality I needed. I can't get Google Docs to automatically open .docx files natively? Really?

Why would you do this? Chrome OS requires a frequent (if not constant) internet connection to be of much use at all. Older devices tend to have poor battery life, so having to use WiFi all the time is an awful idea. A distro using a DE like Cinnamon or MATE will be able to run just as well (if not better) than Chrome OS. You will have all positives of Chrome OS (after all, all you need is a browser in order to do the same stuff) (except for the soon-coming android apps) and none of the downsides (required Google usage, internet dependence).
